discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, establishing moiré quantum matter

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: 2D materials and moiré quantum matter
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene layers to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands almost flat, so that electron interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed the prediction by building magic-angle devices and discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity. The experiments were quickly reproduced by many groups worldwide. Twist angle became a new control knob for quantum matter. Out of this work came moiré physics: tunable correlated phases, orbital magnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and, most recently, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field in twisted and rhombohedral moiré systems. A simple theoretical idea, followed by a decisive experiment, opened a whole field. It gives physicists a clean, gate-tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological physics.
